story.heading:
Every Celebration
Begins With an Idea.
paragraphs: Atithya began with a simple observation — the families who enjoyed their own celebrations most were the ones who weren't managing them.

So we built a studio that takes the whole weight of an event: the concept, the drawings, the vendor contracts, the run sheet and the thousand small decisions nobody warns you about. What we hand back is the part that actually matters — a day you get to be present for.

We take on a limited number of events each season. That's deliberate. It means your florist is briefed by the same person who drew your floor plan, and that on the day itself, someone who knows your family by name is standing quietly at the door.

featured.title: The Courtyard Wedding
featured.body: Three days, two families and a mandap built around a sixty-year-old rain tree. We designed the ceremony, ran guest logistics for 320 people, and delivered a reception that started twenty minutes early.

image.alt: A dessert table styled with lanterns, cake stands and soft neutral linen.

featured.title: A Sky Full of Firsts
featured.body: A pastel afternoon for forty guests — a dessert table in blush and cloud white, a ceremony corner the grandmothers had specifically asked for, and seating that kept every generation talking.

image.alt: A dark private dining table laid with crystal glassware and folded linen.

featured.title: Sixty, Golden
featured.body: A seated dinner for eighty in a private room — brass, ivory linen and deliberately low florals, with a menu built entirely around the meals the guest of honour grew up eating.

image.alt: A candlelit reception room set with long tables and trailing greenery.

featured.title: Annual Partners' Night
featured.body: An awards evening for 250 — stage design, run-of-show, speaker cues and vendor management, held together until the last car pulled away at half past one.

services.title: Event Concept & Planning
services.body: We start with the guest list, the budget and the feeling you're after — then build the concept, the timeline and the cost sheet that everything else is measured against.

services.title: Décor & Styling
services.body: Palette, florals, linen, lighting, signage and tabletop — drawn to scale and sampled in advance, so what arrives on the day is what you approved.

services.title: Venue Setup
services.body: Floor plans, guest flow, stage and seating, power and access. We walk the venue early and solve the awkward corners before they become the day's problem.

services.title: Vendor Coordination
services.body: Catering, photography, sound, entertainment, transport. We brief them, negotiate them, chase them and keep a single schedule that everyone works from.

services.title: Event-Day Management
services.body: A dedicated coordinator and crew on site from load-in to load-out, holding the run sheet so no one in your family has to answer a single vendor call.

services.title: Custom Experiences
services.body: The details people remember — a live counter, a surprise entry, a hand-drawn menu, a ritual reimagined for a room your grandmother would still recognise.

experience.title: Concept
experience.body: We meet, we listen, and we come back with a direction — a palette, a mood and a shape for the day.

experience.title: Planning
experience.body: Budget, venue, guest count and calendar are locked. You get one document that holds every decision.

experience.title: Design
experience.body: Layouts drawn to scale, florals sampled, linen and lighting chosen. Nothing is left to be imagined.

experience.title: Coordination
experience.body: Vendors briefed and contracted, deliveries sequenced, a run sheet circulated to everyone involved.

experience.title: Execution
experience.body: Our crew arrives before anyone else and leaves after everyone else. You simply attend your own celebration.

faqs.question: What types of events do you manage?
faqs.answer: Weddings and all their attendant functions, engagements and roka ceremonies, birthdays from first to eightieth, baby showers, naming ceremonies, anniversaries, house parties and corporate evenings — launches, award nights and offsites. If it involves guests, a room and a timeline, it's within our range.

faqs.question: How far in advance should I book?
faqs.answer: For weddings, six to nine months gives us the best choice of venues and vendors. For birthdays, showers and private dinners, ten to fourteen weeks is comfortable. We do take shorter timelines when the calendar allows — ask, and we'll tell you honestly whether we can do it well.

faqs.question: Do you provide décor and styling?
faqs.answer: Yes — it's the heart of what we do. Concept, palette, florals, linen, lighting, signage, stage and tabletop are all designed in-house and produced with partners we've worked with for years. You'll see layouts and samples before anything is ordered.

faqs.question: Can you work with our preferred venue?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. We're happy to work in a venue you've already chosen — hotel, farmhouse, banquet hall, clubhouse or your own home. We'll do a site visit early, confirm what the venue allows, and design within those constraints. If you haven't chosen yet, we'll shortlist options that suit your guest count and budget.

faqs.question: Can you work within a specific budget?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we'd rather you tell us the real number at the start. We plan within it and show you where every rupee is going in a written cost sheet. Where the budget is tight, we'll tell you which two or three elements will carry the room and where it's safe to spend less.

faqs.question: Do you manage vendors and event-day coordination?
faqs.answer: We do. Catering, photography, sound, lighting, entertainment, transport and staffing are briefed, contracted and scheduled by us. On the day, a dedicated coordinator and crew are on site from load-in to load-out, working from a single run sheet — so no one in your family fields a vendor call.
